    19  # Unramified morphisms
    20  
    21  An `R`-algebra `A` is formally unramified if `Ω[A⁄R]` is trivial.
    22  This is equivalent to the standard definition "for every `R`-algebra,
    23  every square-zero ideal `I : Ideal B` and `f : A →ₐ[R] B ⧸ I`, there exists
    24  at most one lift `A →ₐ[R] B`".
    25  It is unramified if it is formally unramified and of finite type.
    26  
    27  Note that there are multiple definitions in the literature. The definition we give is equivalent to
    28  the one in the Stacks Project https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00US. Note that in EGA unramified
    29  is defined as formally unramified and of finite presentation.
    30  
    31  We show that the property extends onto nilpotent ideals, and that it is stable
    32  under `R`-algebra homomorphisms and compositions.
    33  
    34  We show that unramified is stable under algebra isomorphisms, composition and
    35  localization at an element.
